newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asian Sugar - Thai raw premiums continue to firm.
newsitem.headline: Asian Sugar - Thai raw premiums continue to firm.

text.p: Thai raw sugar premiums are continuing to firm due to concerns about an unseasonable dry spell in Thailand that is damaging crops and tightening supplies, Japanese traders said on Friday.
But they also said rainfall this week in sugar producing areas in Thailand was expected to weigh the topside.

On Friday, Thai raw sugar premiums for July-September deliveries were quoted at around 90/100 points (bid/offer) per pound over New York's Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange futures on an FOB basis, compared to 80/90 a week earlier.

"The dry weather has aggravated concern over Thai's production, pushing up premiums," a sugar trader at a major trade house said. "But as it rained there this week, we'd like to assess how the situation has changed. Traders are now taking a wait-and-see attitude," he said.
Traders also said they were watching how temperatures in Japan this summer would affect sugar consumption.
The Meteorological Agency said last month that temperatures during the three months from July to September are likely to be average to lower than average in Japan.
"Cool weather will dent sugar demand for drinks and ice cream," another trader said.
